classification.difficultyReason: Follow a supplied ground-plane sine-rule expression into a vertical right-triangle height calculation.

content.prompt:
Two observers at $A$ and $B$ on horizontal ground are 300 m apart.

From $A$, the angle of elevation of the top $C$ of a tall building $DC$ is $32^\circ$.

It is also known that $\angle DAB=59^\circ$ and $\angle ADB=78^\circ$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 19, perspective building diagram below part b
spec.description: Perspective triangle ACB with A lower left, B lower right, C above internal point D. AC, CB and AB are solid. AD, DB and DC are dashed. Height h lies to the right of DC; 300 m lies below AB. Cyan adjacent elevation and ground-angle sectors at A carry 32° and 59°; the cyan ground-angle sector at D carries 78°. Preserve the outlined perpendicular marker at D and the source vertex labels.
spec.mathematics: AB=300 m; angle CAD=32°; angle DAB=59°; angle ADB=78°; CD=h and CD is perpendicular to the ground plane ADB. The source is a foreshortened perspective view, not a scale plan.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence find the height of the building, correct to the nearest metre.
